title: Brown Sugar Cinnamon Swirl Cupcakes
shortDescription: Warm brown sugar cupcakes with a baked in cinnamon swirl, ready in 25 minutes prep and 18 minutes bake.
description: These cupcakes taste like a snickerdoodle and a coffee cake had a baby. The batter uses brown sugar instead of white, so it bakes up soft and a little caramel toned. A ribbon of cinnamon sugar gets swirled through the middle before baking, so every bite has that warm cinnamon pocket. I tested this batch three times in my home kitchen to get the swirl to stay put instead of sinking to the bottom. The vanilla cinnamon frosting on top ties it all together without tasting like a plain vanilla cupcake.
ingredients: 1/4 cup packed light brown sugar (for swirl)
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F. Line a 12 cup muffin pan with paper liners.
Whisk flour, baking powder, and salt in a medium bowl. Set aside.
Beat butter and brown sugar together for 2 minutes until fluffy and light in color.
Add eggs one at a time, beating well after each. Mix in vanilla extract.
Add flour mixture and milk in three parts, alternating, starting and ending with flour. Mix just until combined.
In a small bowl, stir together the swirl brown sugar and cinnamon until it looks like wet sand.
Fill each liner halfway with batter. Sprinkle 1 teaspoon of the cinnamon swirl mix on top of each.
Cover with remaining batter, then drag a toothpick through each cup in a swirl pattern to marble the mixture.
Bake 17 to 19 minutes, until a toothpick in the center comes out clean. Cool in the pan 5 minutes, then move to a wire rack.
For frosting, beat cream cheese and butter together until smooth. Add powdered sugar, cinnamon, and vanilla, then beat 3 minutes until fluffy.
Once cupcakes are fully cool, pipe frosting in a swirl on top of each cupcake.
tips: Room temperature eggs and milk blend faster and give a smoother crumb, so set them out 30 minutes early.
Do not overmix once the flour goes in. Overmixed batter makes the cinnamon swirl sink instead of staying marbled.
Chill the frosting for 10 minutes if it feels too soft to pipe a tall swirl.
Use light brown sugar for a milder caramel taste, or dark brown sugar for a deeper, richer flavor.

faq.question: Why did my cinnamon swirl sink to the bottom of the cupcake?
faq.answer: This happens when the swirl mix is too heavy or the batter is too thin. Keep the cinnamon sugar mix dry and only drag a toothpick through once or twice, not stirred all the way in.

faq.question: Can I use dark brown sugar instead of light brown sugar?
faq.answer: Yes, dark brown sugar works well here and gives a deeper molasses taste. The cupcakes will look slightly darker but bake the same way.

faq.question: How far ahead can I bake these cupcakes?
faq.answer: Bake the unfrosted cupcakes up to 2 days ahead and store in an airtight container at room temperature. Frost them the day you plan to serve for the best texture.

faq.question: Can I make these without cream cheese in the frosting?
faq.answer: Swap the cream cheese for an extra 4 tablespoons of butter for a simple vanilla cinnamon buttercream. The frosting will be a bit sweeter and less tangy.

conclusion: These cupcakes bring cozy snickerdoodle flavor into a soft, swirled cupcake. The cinnamon ribbon inside makes each bite a little different, which is half the fun. Try them for a fall bake sale or just a Sunday afternoon baking project.
